chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Sahl ibn Ziyad, altogether from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Muhammad ibn Abdullah al-Qummi, who said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) about the man who is given the money for Hajj; he performs Hajj with it and spends liberally upon himself, and there remains an excess from it. Should he return it to him? He (peace be upon him) said: No, it is for him.

key_terms.الْحَجَّةَ: The money or funds designated for performing Hajj
key_terms.هِيَ لَهُ: It is for him / It belongs to him
key_terms.يَفْضُلُ مِنْهَا: There remains an excess/surplus from it
key_terms.يُوَسِّعُ عَلَى نَفْسِهِ: He spends liberally upon himself / expands his own spending

ai.seo_question: What happens to the leftover money from Hajj funds if the performer spends more than given or keeps the excess?
ai.summary: In this hadith from Al-Kafi, Imam al-Rida (AS) clarifies the fiqh of Hajj funds, ruling that if a person is given money to perform Hajj and spends it or retains the surplus, the excess belongs to them as a gift, not as a trust requiring return. This ruling highlights the distinction between the obligation of the ritual and the ownership of the provided resources, a key point in Shia jurisprudence regarding voluntary Hajj (Hajj al-Tatawwu'). It underscores the generosity of the giver and the autonomy of the performer once the funds are utilized for the pilgrimage.
